gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's F3800 Plus page says '240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC', so a 120V TT-30 portable generator recharging it during a long Texas outage switches off 240V loads like central AC. BLUETTI says its Apex 300 powers 120V and 240V devices 'even while charging', and sells a Home Integration Kit that it lists as compatible with the Apex 300 only.
standout_why: I compared against theenergycollective.com/home-battery-backup (cited). It covers only the EcoFlow Delta Pro Ultra, plus the Delta Pro 3 with Smart Home Panel 2. It says nothing about 240V while charging, generator voltage or kit-to-model pairing, and it doesn't mention Anker or BLUETTI. I didn't open homebattery.guide, ocsolar.com or solarexaminer.com. Going by their titles and ChatGPT's answer, they compare Powerwall 3, Enphase 10C and FranklinWH, and ChatGPT's EcoFlow card only says integration 'can still require an electrician and additional equipment'. None of these pairs a generator with a 240V output. I scored 2, not 3: the BLUETTI half of the contrast is a marketing claim with no test behind it, and the Apex 300 ships in late January.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W). BLUETTI says it powers 120V and 240V devices at the same time, even while charging, so a 240V circuit can stay on while a generator recharges it.
Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K. Paired with the Apex 300 it gives 5,529.6 Wh in BLUETTI's own bundle (B500K is the other battery BLUETTI names for this unit).

Home connection: BLUETTI Apex 300 Home Integration Kit, 'Single Apex 300' variant. BLUETTI lists 'Compatible Models: Apex300'. The AC500, AC300, EP500Pro and EP900/EP800 kits are separate SKUs for other models, and a 'Parallel' variant ($799) is for linked units. An electrician still has to wire it to the main panel.
Rejected: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus. The Anker store shows it Sold Out with no price, Amazon returned nothing, and its 120V-charging rule cuts 240V output, which breaks the generator-recharge plan.

findings.label: 240V output while charging on 120V AC
findings.value: Not available: '240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: Maker's US page. This is the deciding exclusion for a plan that recharges from a common 120V portable generator during an outage while running 240V loads.

findings.label: 120V generator input
findings.value: Through the generator's TT-30R outlet, up to 3,000 W; must be pure sine wave with THD under 5%
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: Maker's page. AC charging is listed as 1,800 W max and bypass as 1,440 W max.

findings.label: 240V generator path (HPP & Generator Adapter port)
findings.value: 6,000 W max AC input; needs the Anker SOLIX Generator Adapter and works with a single F3800 Plus only
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: Maker's footnote: '*Anker SOLIX Generator Adapter required and only support single F3800 Plus unit.'

findings.label: 240V outlet
findings.value: L14-30R, 120V/240V, 25 A max, 6,000 W max (no NEMA 14-50; the page's comparison table lists 14-50 only on the standard F3800)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: The page shows Sold Out and 'Price Loading'.

findings.label: Rooftop solar during an outage
findings.value: Cannot recharge through the Home Power Panel during an outage; 11–165V panels must connect directly to the unit
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page (FAQ)
findings.note: Maker's FAQ. Up to 6 BP3800 batteries (3.84 kWh each). 5-year warranty.

findings.label: 120V + 240V while charging
findings.value: 'power both 120V and 240V devices simultaneously — even while charging'
findings.note: Maker's claim. The page gives no wattage at 240V and doesn't name the ports beyond 'AC input 15A, AC output 30A/50A, and 50A in/out ports'.

findings.label: Generator / AC charging input
findings.note: The page doesn't say whether this figure is for one unit or for 2–3 linked units. The rear-panel label on the same page reads AC input 15A.

findings.source_title: Apex 300 Home Integration Kit – BLUETTI US
